title: The $50 million deal Blockbuster said no to 📼
subject: blockbuster
description:
Would you have said yes? 👇

In 2000, Netflix's founders flew to Dallas and offered to sell Netflix to Blockbuster for $50 million. Here's how the biggest no in business history played out.

Sources: Reed Hastings, No Rules Rules (excerpt via Marketplace), Yahoo Finance interview (2020), Newsweek fact check, CNNMoney (2010), StockAnalysis (Netflix market cap, Oct 1 2026)

scenes.text: Blockbuster could have bought Netflix for 50 million dollars.
It was 2000. Netflix was a 2-year-old startup mailing DVDs, and it lost 57 million dollars that year.
Blockbuster had nearly 9,000 stores. In a Dallas office, Netflix's founders say CEO John Antioco heard the price and said no.
But here's the strange part. Reed Hastings later said, thank God they didn't. 10 years later, Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy.
